identity.name: compute_centroids
identity.description: Fills parcels.centroid_lat/centroid_lng for every parcel with a geometry and no centroid yet — ONE server-side conditional UPDATE ... WHERE geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NULL RETURNING id (PostGIS ST_Centroid), never revisits an already-filled row. Migration 245's trigger, a SEPARATE mechanism, is what makes a row eligible again after a geometry change.

why_lock.text: Lock 99 is not the spec number — it is Spec 47 §A.5's registry id (row 5, "Maintenance" wave, "Writes Timestamps? NO"), unrelated to either owning spec's own number (43 or 55). Kept textually per §5.4 so the registry loop (src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts) stays green across the conversion — this step has carried lock 99 since commit 3c3e6f84 (2026-04-16) and nothing about the conversion changes it.

guard_why.text: The WHERE clause (`centroid_lat IS NULL`) IS the scope, not a value-change guard — an already-filled row is permanently ineligible for this step's own UPDATE regardless of which algorithm filled it; only migration 245's trigger (a different write path entirely) makes a row eligible again. An IS DISTINCT FROM guard on a NULL-scoped row is vacuous: there is nothing to compare against. Grandfathered in scripts/steps/_schema/grandfathered.json (Rule 9), keyed on write_discipline.guard, not .class.

guard_columns_why.text: LG-9 escape hatch, moot here (mirrors link_parcel_addresses' own note): guard is "none", so guard_columns is never consulted to build an IS DISTINCT FROM clause. Neither column declares columns[].source "run_at" (this write target has no timestamp column at all, Spec 47 §A.5 "Writes Timestamps? NO"), so the LG-9 trap this field exists to catch cannot occur here either way.

write_discipline.scope: geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NULL

why.text: LG-20 (this pilot). A single conditional UPDATE, no batching in the surviving (PostGIS-only) path after A-1(a) retires the JS fallback — the scope predicate is the entire write contract, and it self-excludes on every subsequent run (idempotent_rerun: zero_writes, proven by the twice-run acceptance test at migration-245-centroid-invalidation.db.test.ts case (4)).

invalidates.when: migration 245's trigger NULLs this column on any geom UPDATE (IS DISTINCT FROM) — documents 245's mechanism as it bears on this step's own eligibility scope; 245's trigger, not this step, does the invalidating (G3: this step's contract stays "fill what's NULL")
migration 245's trigger NULLs this column on any geom UPDATE (IS DISTINCT FROM) — same mechanism as centroid_lat, declared per-column per the schema's own {table,column,when} shape

why.text: One write target, one write statement, no batching in the surviving path — the single conditional UPDATE ... WHERE geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NULL RETURNING id (LG-20's executeBackfillUpdate). The simplest write shape of any pilot converted to date.

staleness.scope: geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NULL

why.text: A-1(a) (this pilot). The JS arithmetic-mean fallback (and the CC-D1 cursor-pagination fence it carried) is RETIRED WHOLE, not kept-declared-unreachable — a database with no PostGIS extension now HALTS rather than silently switching to a second algorithm with a different centroid formula (Finding 7, algorithm-drift: PostGIS ST_Centroid is area-weighted, the retired JS fallback was an unweighted arithmetic mean of ring vertices). Per the link_massing A-8 precedent.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value the library already measured — a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition. It must redden the run, not drop its row.

expect.reports: the pre-run count of parcels with a geometry and no centroid yet — the eligibility scope's own denominator

why.text: R-P's spirit (N/A — this BACKFILL declares no ledger gate to narrow checks around, so R-P itself does not apply): a data-driven zero-work completion must still persist WHY it had nothing to do, the same way a gated skip's gate_decision row does on every other archetype. Declared when:"pre" so it is scored even on the zero-work path.

why.text: T1 (Spec 124 Rule 3). Ported verbatim from the pre-conversion script's own literal threshold (`:197`, `== 0`, WARN not FAIL — a malformed geometry is a data-quality signal, never a reason to halt the run). Default 0, bounds 0-10000, on_invalid "fail" (verdict-affecting, R-G).

expect.of: centroids_computed / parcels_processed — a floor on the fraction of the eligible scope that actually computed

why.text: T2 (Spec 124 Rule 3). Ported verbatim from the pre-conversion script's own literal threshold (`:198`,`:200`, `>= 98%`). The default (98) is NOT an arbitrary literal — it traces to commit d32612bb's deliberate business-accuracy tightening ("tighten compute_rate from 90% to 98%"), cited by SHA rather than treated as unexplained. Bounds 0-100, on_invalid "fail" (verdict-affecting, R-G).

R-T addendum, commit 4 (net-new, 0/7 golden entries overlap an existing declared check — compute_centroids has only 2 bound checks, neither about centroid VALUE correctness). Pure telemetry, value_min 0 sanity floor. 56ms median, 3 timings, single session.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NULL

why.text: R-T addendum, commit 4 (net-new). A parcel with a real polygon but no computed centroid is exactly the backlog compute_centroids exists to drain (this step's own `backlog_count`/`compute_rate` checks measure the RATE, not this residual count directly) — WARN, not FAIL, since a standing backlog tail is expected between runs, not a defect. 638ms median, 3 timings, single session.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE geometry IS NOT NULL AND geom IS NULL

why.text: R-T addendum, commit 4 (net-new). `geom` (PostGIS) is derived from `geometry` (GeoJSON) upstream of this step (migration 242's own trigger) — a non-zero count here means that derivation broke, not something this step's own scope could fix, but a genuine upstream-health signal worth carrying on this step's own audit row (this step is the first consumer of geom that would notice). WARN: visible every run, never blocks. 13ms median, 3 timings, single session.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NOT NULL AND NOT ST_Contains(geom, ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(centroid_lng, centroid_lat),4326))

why.text: R-T addendum, commit 4 (net-new). A computed centroid physically outside its own parcel's polygon (concave-lot drift, the CC-D2/CC-D3 defect class) — measured live, standing non-zero (3,626), never zero by design under this step's own scope (WHERE centroid_lat IS NULL only, never revisits a filled row per its own §1.10 profile) — WARN + effectively a standing residual, consistent with the CC-D2/CC-D3 root-cause finding filed HIGH/PIN in review_followups. Not FAIL: the same standing-non-zero-by-design rule (Spec 48 §4.9) LM-D6/LM-D11 use. 515ms median, 3 timings, single session.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NOT NULL AND ST_DistanceSphere(ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(centroid_lng, centroid_lat),4326), ST_PointOnSurface(geom)) > 1.0

why.text: R-T addendum, commit 4 (net-new). Distance from the stored centroid to a GUARANTEED-on-polygon reference point (ST_PointOnSurface, distinct from the ST_Centroid comparison below — this one never falls off a concave lot by construction). Standing non-zero (298,021 of 486,530, 61.3%) is the same CC-D2/CC-D3 class as outside_polygon_count above — WARN, self-retires only via a future one-time recompute-FULL (filed, not this step's own scope). 1,066ms median, 3 timings, single session.

invariants.sql: WITH drifted AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT id, geom, ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(centroid_lng, centroid_lat), 4326) AS c FROM parcels WHERE geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NOT NULL AND NOT ST_Contains(geom, ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(centroid_lng, centroid_lat), 4326))) SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS c FROM drifted d CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT p2.id FROM parcels p2 WHERE ST_Contains(p2.geom, d.c) AND p2.id <> d.id LIMIT 1) hit

why.text: R-T addendum, commit 4 (net-new). The SHARPEST tail of outside_polygon_count above: a drifted centroid that lands not just off its own lot but INSIDE A DIFFERENT parcel entirely — the exact class link-parcels.js's Tier-3 nearest-centroid join is exposed to (RT-CC3, filed review_followups). 3,130 of 3,626 outside-polygon centroids (86.3%) land in a neighbour. WARN, same standing-residual reasoning. 597ms median, 3 timings, single session.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NOT NULL AND ST_DistanceSphere(ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(centroid_lng, centroid_lat),4326), ST_Centroid(geom)) > 1.0
plausibility.retighten_when: zero rows (would require a one-time recompute-FULL under today's PostGIS algorithm, filed not built — CC-D3)

why.text: R-T addendum, commit 4 — this is CC-D3 (defect-ledger.md, filed 2026-08-29), the plan's own worked example for plausibility[] vs invariants[]: the bound is 'computed <= 1m from a value populated by a DIFFERENT run' (this step's own scope is WHERE centroid_lat IS NULL, so it never revisits an already-filled row — the drift is inherited, not created, by any given run), not a value this step's own write could self-correct. Measured live: 292,587/486,530 (60.1%) differ from a freshly-computed ST_Centroid(geom) by >1m on the SAME unchanged geom — matches CC-D3's own filed figure exactly. PHYSICAL-BOUND (Fold A-5): grounded in a real geometric recomputation, not a telemetry trend. WARN + retighten_when, never FAIL — self-retires only via CC-D3's own filed one-time recompute-FULL recommendation. 1,182ms median, 3 timings, single session.

limitations.what: CC-D2 (Reality-Check R-1, pinned): of 3,626 out-of-polygon centroids, 3,130 land inside a DIFFERENT parcel, exposing a 276-link mis-attribution signature in link-parcels.js's Tier-3 nearest-centroid join. This step's own output (the centroid value itself) is correct per its own contract (ST_Centroid computes exactly what it is asked to compute, Spec 59 R2.5 rules a concave-lot centroid outside its own polygon is correct-by-design) — the exposure is in a DOWNSTREAM consumer's join strategy, not in compute_centroids. PINNED for this pilot (zero-behaviour-change scope); HIGH followup filed against link_parcels.js.
limitations.measured: 3,626/486,530 (0.75%) outside-polygon; 3,130 land inside a neighbour parcel; 276/494 spatial-tier permit_parcels links point at a drifted parcel (2026-08-29 session)

limitations.what: CC-D3 (Finding 7, pinned): 292,587/486,530 (60.1%) of stored centroids differ >1m from a freshly-computed ST_Centroid over the SAME unchanged geom — root cause is algorithm drift (the one real-work run, 2026-03-10, predates the PostGIS offload and used the retired JS arithmetic-mean formula; the remainder predates pipeline_runs ledger visibility entirely, most plausibly a bulk seed/restore). This step's own G1 guarantee ("fills centroid for every parcel with a geometry and no centroid yet") never promised WHICH formula, and the scope predicate makes an already-filled row permanently out of this step's own reach by design, not by oversight. Filed MED (below CC-D2's HIGH — no measured downstream mis-link count for this finding).
limitations.measured: 292,587/486,530 (60.1%) stored-vs-fresh centroid distance > 1m; avg 6.61m, median 4.12m, max 1,476.84m (2026-08-29 session)

recovery.reset: No TRUNCATE/rebuild mechanism exists. A re-run re-scans the full geom IS NOT NULL AND centroid_lat IS NULL scope, which is already the CORRECT reset behaviour for a class-E write_once_backfill target — the scope predicate self-excludes every already-filled row, so there is no separate destructive rebuild path to declare. This IS, in effect, migration 245's own trigger: nulling centroid_lat re-admits a row to this step's scope, which is the only "reset" this step's own contract recognizes.

interrupted_why.text: No destructive retraction target exists on this step (class E, retract:"none") — there is nothing for an interrupted run to leave half-retracted. A crashed mid-UPDATE run simply leaves whatever subset the single server-side statement had already committed (statement-level atomicity — Postgres either commits the whole UPDATE or none of it); a re-run picks up exactly where the scope leaves off. R-F item 1 (carried forward, same disposition as pilot 5): this pilot does NOT itself exercise or close R-B's crashed/stuck-running reader gap.

before_image_why.text: R-M/LG-17's before-image mechanism applies to a destructive retraction; this step has none (class E, retract:"none"). The UPDATE is additive-in-place (NULL -> a computed float) and reversible by re-nulling the same two columns if ever needed, which is not the same hazard class a before-image protects against.

why.text: The normal outcome: eligible rows existed (backlog_count > 0) and the UPDATE ran.

The steady-state outcome measured on every recorded live run since 2026-06-10: backlog_count == 0, the UPDATE is never issued, only when:"pre" checks are scored. NOT a skip_gated terminal (R-P N/A) — this is a normal completion, not a ledger-gated skip.
A WARN row stands (failed_geometries or compute_rate) and nothing FAILED — the run completed and wrote; the warning is in the table.
Advisory lock 99 is held by another process — a row-derived SKIP summary, never a bare SDK skip with no audit_table.
